sections.description:
Find and execute a Lua source file, but continue without error if the file is not present.

```lua
dofileopt("filename")
```
sections.parameters: `fname` is the name of the file to load. This may be specified as a single file path or an array of file paths, in which case the first file found is run.
sections.returns: True if a file was found and executed, nil otherwise.

sections.description:
The **iif** function implements an immediate "if" clause, returning one of two possible values.

```lua
result = iif(condition, trueval, falseval)
```
sections.parameters: *condition* is the logical condition to test. *trueval* is the value to return if the condition evaluates to true, *falseval* if the condition evaluates false.
sections.returns: *trueval* is the condition evaluates true, *falseval* otherwise.
sections.examples:
```lua
result = iif(os.is("windows"), "is windows", "is not windows")
```

Note that all expressions are evaluated before the condition is checked; the following expression can not be implemented with an immediate if because it may try to concatenate a string value.

```lua
result = iif(x ~= nil, "x is " .. x, "x is nil")
```

sections.description:
Looks for and executes another script file, if it hasn't been run previously.

```lua
include("path")
```
sections.parameters:
`path` is the file system path to a script file or a directory. If a directory is specified, Premake looks for a file named `premake5.lua` in that directory and runs it if found.

If the file or directory specified has already been included previously, the call is ignored. If you want to execute the same script multiple times, use Lua's [dofile()](http://www.lua.org/manual/5.1/manual.html#pdf-dofile) instead.
sections.returns: Any values returned by the included script are passed through to the caller.
sections.examples:
```lua
-- runs "src/MyApplication/premake5.lua"
include "src/MyApplication"

-- runs "my_script.lua" just once
include "my_script.lua"
include "my_script.lua"
```

sections.description:
Evaluates a script, and marks any containers created by that script as external.

```lua
includeexternal("path")
```

For complex multi-workspace builds, it can be advantageous to have a set of projects that are generated by one workspace, and then used by the other workspaces as-is, without regenerating.

With this function, you can include a script which may contain one or more project or rule definitions. All such containers will be marked as external, and simply referenced, but not regenerated.
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to a script file or a directory. See [include()](include.md) for a more complete description.

sections.description:
The `printf` performs like its C counterpart, printing a formatted string.

```lua
printf("format", ...)
```

It is equivalent to this Lua code:

```lua
print(string.format(format, unpack(arg))
```
sections.parameters: **format** is a formatting string containing C `printf()` style formatting codes. It is followed by a list of arguments to be substituted into the format string.

sections.description:
An extension of [Lua's require() function](http://www.lua.org/pil/8.1.html) which adds support for Premake modules and version checking.

```lua
require ("modname", "versions")
```

Premake will use its [extended set of module locations](Locating-Scripts.md) when locating the requested module.
sections.parameters:
`modname` is the name of the module to be loaded. See [Locating Scripts](Locating-Scripts.md) for more information about how Premake modules are located.

`versions` is an optional string of a version requirements. See the examples below for more information on the format of the requirements string. If the requirements are not met, an error will be raised.
sections.returns: The module object.
sections.examples:
Require Premake version 5.0 or later.

```lua
require("premake", ">=5.0")
```

If no operator is specified, defaults to ">=". I think it is a little more readable to include it though.

```lua
require("premake", "5.0")
```

Require a version 5.0 alpha 3 or later.

```lua
require("premake", ">=5.0.0-alpha3")
```

Require anything between Premake version 5.1 and 6.0.

```lua
require("premake", ">=5.0 <6.0")
```

The same rules apply to third-party modules.

```lua
require("foo", ">=1.1")
```

sections.description:
The `verbosef` performs `printf`, printing a formatted string, but only when the **verbose** flag was set (ex. in the command line).

```lua
verbosef("format", ...)
```
sections.parameters: **format** is a formatting string containing C `printf()` style formatting codes. It is followed by a list of arguments to be substituted into the format string.

sections.description:
Downloads an HTTP resource from the specified URL to a file.

```lua
http.download(url, file, { options })
```
sections.parameters:
`url` is the URL to be downloaded.

`file` is the destination file that will be written to.

`options` is a [table of options](http-options-table.md) used for this HTTP request.
sections.returns:
There are two return values.

```lua
result_str, response_code = http.download(url, file, { options })
```

 * `result_str` is set to "OK" if successful or contains a description of the failure.
 * `result_code` is the HTTP [result code](http://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec10.html) of the download.

sections.description:
Perform a HTTP GET request using the specified URL.

```lua
http.get(url, { options })
```
sections.parameters:
`url` is the URL to be downloaded.

`options` is a [table of options](http-options-table.md) used for this HTTP request.
sections.returns:
There are three return values.

```lua
resource, result_str, response_code = http.get(url, { options })
```

 * `resource` is the content that was retrieved or nil if it could not be retrieved.
 * `result_str` is set to "OK" if successful or contains a description of the failure.
 * `result_code` is the HTTP [result code](http://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec10.html) of the get.

sections.description:
Perform a HTTP POST request to the specified URL.

```lua
http.post(url, data, { options })
```
sections.parameters:
`url` is the URL to POST to.

`data` is a string containing the data to post.

`options` is a [table of options](http-options-table.md) used for this HTTP request.
sections.returns:
There are three return values.

```lua
resource, result_str, response_code = http.post(url, data, { options })
```

 * `resource` is the content that was retrieved or nil if it could not be retrieved.
 * `result_str` is set to "OK" if successful or contains a description of the failure.
 * `result_code` is the HTTP [result code](http://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec10.html) of the get.
sections.examples:
```lua
local resource, result_str, response_code = http.post("http://example.com/api.json", "somedata")
```

sections.description:
Decodes a JSON string into a table.

```lua
result, err = json.decode("s")
```
sections.parameters: `s` is the string to decode.
sections.returns:
`result` is the resulting table, or `nil` on failure

`err` is the error message if there is one available, always set to `nil` on success

sections.description:
Encodes a table to JSON.

```lua
result, err = json.encode(tbl)
```
sections.parameters: `tbl` is the table to encode.
sections.returns:
`result` is the resulting string, or `nil` on failure

`err` is the error message if there is one available, always set to `nil` on success

sections.description:
Encodes a table to JSON with spacing and tabulation.

```lua
result, err = json.encode_pretty(tbl)
```
sections.parameters: `tbl` is the table to encode.
sections.returns:
`result` is the resulting string, or `nil` on failure

`err` is the error message if there is one available, always set to `nil` on success

sections.description:
Changes the current working directory.

```lua
ok, err = os.chdir("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to the new working directory.
sections.returns: **True** if successful, otherwise **nil** and an error message.

sections.description:
Changes the file system permissions of a file.

```lua
ok, err = os.chmod(path, mask)
```
sections.parameters:
`path` is the path to the file on which the permissions should be changed.

`mask` is a string specifying the new permission mask. Currently, only octal number notations is supported, e.g. "755".
sections.returns: If successful, returns true. On error, returns nil and an error message.

sections.description:
Compares two files for binary equality.

```lua
equality, err = os.comparefiles("filename1", "filename2")
```
sections.parameters:
`filename1` is the file system path to the first file to compare file.

`filename2` is the file system path to the second file to compare file.
sections.returns: True if the file are identical by content, false if not, returns nil and an error message if an error occurred.

sections.description:
Copies a file from one location to another.

```lua
ok, err = os.copyfile("source", "destination")
```
sections.parameters:
`source` is the file system path to the file to be copied.

`destination` is the path to the copy location.
sections.returns: **True** if successful, otherwise **nil** and an error message.

sections.description:
Execute a system command

```lua
os.execute("command")
```

Execute a system command, just like `os.execute()`, but accepting a format string and values as arguments.

```lua
os.executef("format", ...)
```
sections.parameters: `format` is a printf-style formatting string (see Lua's [string.format()](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/1811884/lua-string-format-options) for examples), followed by a corresponding list of values for token substitution.
sections.returns: The return value of the executed command.

sections.description:
Scan the well-known system locations looking for a header file.

```lua
p = os.findheader("headerfile" [, additionalpaths])
```
sections.parameters:
`headerfile` is a file name or a the end of a file path to locate.

`additionalpaths` is a string or a table of one or more additional search path.
sections.returns: The path containing the header file, if found. Otherwise, nil.
sections.remarks: `os.findheader` mostly use the same paths as [[os.findlib]] but replace `/lib` by `/include`.

sections.description:
Scan the well-known system locations looking for a library file.

```lua
p = os.findlib("libname" [, additionalpaths])
```

This function does not work to locate system libraries on macOS 11 or later; it may still be used to locate user libraries. From [the release notes](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/macos-release-notes/macos-big-sur-11_0_1-release-notes):

> New in macOS Big Sur 11.0.1, the system ships with a built-in dynamic linker cache of all system-provided libraries. As part of this change, copies of dynamic libraries are no longer present on the filesystem. Code that attempts to check for dynamic library presence by looking for a file at a path or enumerating a directory will fail.
sections.parameters:
`libname` is name of the library to locate. It may be specified with (`libX11.so`) or without (`X11`) system-specific decorations.

`additionalpaths` is a string or a table of one or more additional search path.
sections.returns: The path containing the library file, if found. Otherwise, nil.
sections.availability: Premake 4.0 or later. Non-macOS host systems only.

sections.description:
Identify the currently targeted operating system.

```lua
id = os.get()
```
sections.returns:
An operating system identifier; see [system()](system.md) for a complete list of identifiers.

Note that this function returns the OS being targeted, which is not necessarily the same as the OS on which Premake is being run. If you are running on Mac OS X and generating Visual Studio project files, the identifier is "Windows", since that is the OS being targeted by the Visual Studio action.
sections.examples:
```lua
if os.get() == "windows" then
   -- do something Windows-specific
end
```

sections.description:
Gets the current working directory.

```lua
cwd = os.getcwd()
```
sections.returns: The full path to the current working directory.

sections.description:
Gets the value of an environment variable from the host system.

```lua
id = os.getenv(var)
```
sections.parameters: `var` Environment variable name.
sections.returns: Returns the value of the environment variable if one is set, or nil.
sections.examples:
```lua
if os.getenv('FOO') == "bar" then
   -- do something specific when FOO=bar
end
```

sections.description:
Gets the number of logical CPU cores.

```lua
os.getnumcpus()
```
sections.returns: The number of logical CPU cores of the running system.

sections.description:
Prompt the user to enter a password.

```lua
password = os.getpass('please enter your password:')
```
sections.parameters: The prompt to display the user.
sections.returns: The password that was entered by the user.

sections.description:
Returns the list of tags corresponding to a system.

There are tags specific to each operating system (see [system()](system.md) for a complete list of identifiers.),
and meta tags like `posix`, `darwin`, `desktop` and `mobile` tags.
sections.tags:
| OS       | Tags                                    |
|----------|-----------------------------------------|
| aix      | aix, posix, desktop                     |
| android  | android, mobile                         |
| bsd      | bsd, posix, desktop                     |
| haiku    | haiku, posix, desktop                   |
| ios      | ios, darwin, posix, mobile              |
| linux    | linux, posix, desktop                   |
| macosx   | macosx, darwin, posix, desktop          |
| solaris  | solaris, posix, desktop                 |
| tvos     | tvos, darwin, posix, mobile             |
| uwp      | uwp, windows, desktop                   |
| windows  | windows, win32, desktop                 |
sections.examples:
```lua
print("iOS system tags: " .. table.concat(os.getSystemTags("ios"), ", "))
-- iOS system tags: ios, darwin, posix, mobile
```

sections.description:
Retrieve version information for the host operating system.

```lua
sysinfo = os.getversion()
```
sections.returns:
A table, containing the following key-value pairs:

| Field         | Description                                       |
|---------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| majorversion  | The major version number                          |
| minorversion  | The minor version number                          |
| revision      | The bug fix release or service pack number        |
| description   | A human-readable description of the OS version    |

On platforms where this function has not been implemented, it will return zero for all version numbers, and the platform name as the description.
sections.examples:
```lua
local ver = os.getversion()
print(string.format(" %d.%d.%d (%s)",
   ver.majorversion, ver.minorversion, ver.revision,
   ver.description))

-- On Windows XP: "5.1.3 (Windows XP)"
-- On OS X,: "10.6.6 (Mac OS X Snow Leopard)"
```

sections.description:
Identify the currently executing operating system.

```lua
id = os.host()
```
sections.returns:
An operating system identifier; see [system()](system.md) for a complete list of identifiers.

Note that this function returns the OS that Premake is currently running on, which is not necessarily the same as the OS that Premake is generating files for. If you are running on Mac OS X and generating Visual Studio project files, the identifier is "macosx".
sections.examples:
```lua
if os.host() == "windows" then
   -- do something Windows-specific
end
```

sections.description:
Identify the architecture for the currently executing operating system.

```lua
id = os.hostarch()
```
sections.returns:
An architecture identifier; see [architecture()](architecture.md) for a complete list of identifiers.

:::warning
Currently, this function actually returns the architecture of the system that Premake was compiled for. This means that if you run the Win32 version of Premake on a 64-bit Windows system, this function will return 'x86' instead of 'x86_64'.
:::
sections.examples:
```lua
if os.hostarch() == "x86_64" then
   -- do something x64-specific
end
```

sections.description:
:::caution
**This function has been deprecated.** Use [os.istarget()](os.istarget.md), [os.target()](os.target.md), or [os.host()](os.host.md) instead.
:::

Checks the current operating system identifier against a particular value.

```lua
os.is("id")
```
sections.parameters:
`id` is an operating system identifier; see [system()](system.md) for a complete list of identifiers.

Note that this function tests against the OS being targeted, which is not necessarily the same as the OS on which Premake is being run. If you are running on Mac OS X and generating Visual Studio project files, the identifier is "Windows", since that is the OS being targeted by the Visual Studio action.
sections.returns: **True** if the supplied ID matches the current operating system identifier, **false** otherwise.

sections.description:
Determines if the host is using a 64-bit processor.

```lua
os.is64bit()
```
sections.returns: **True** if the host system has a 64-bit processor, **false** otherwise.
sections.examples:
```lua
if os.is64bit() then
   print("This is a 64-bit system")
else
   print("This is NOT a 64-bit system")
end
```

sections.description:
Checks for the existence of directory.

```lua
os.isdir("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to check.
sections.returns: **True** if a matching directory is found; **false** is there is no such file system path, or if the path points to a file instead of a directory.

sections.description:
Checks for the existence of file.

```lua
os.isfile("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to check.
sections.returns: **True** if a matching file is found; **false** is there is no such file system path, or if the path points to a directory instead of a file.

sections.description:
Determines if the given path is a symlink or reparse point.

```lua
os.islink(path)
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the path to the file or directory to be checked.
sections.returns: Returns true if the path represents a symlink or Windows reparse point; false otherwise.

sections.description:
Checks the target operating system against a particular identifier or tag.
See [os.getSystemTags](os.getSystemTags.md) for documentation about OS tags.
sections.examples:
```lua
print("Android: " .. os.istarget("android"))
print("Mobile: " .. os.istarget("mobile"))
print("Desktop: " .. os.istarget("desktop"))
```

sections.description:
Creates a new symbolic link to a directory.

```lua
os.linkdir("src", "dst")
```
sections.parameters:
`src` is the path of the directory to create a symbolic link to.
`dst` is the path to the created symbolic link.
sections.returns: True if successful, otherwise nil and an error message.

sections.description:
Creates a new symbolic link to a file.

```lua
os.linkfile("src", "dst")
```
sections.parameters:
`src` is the path of the file to create a symbolic link to.
`dst` is the path to the created symbolic link.
sections.returns: True if successful, otherwise nil and an error message.

sections.description:
Searches the [Premake path](Locating-Scripts.md) for files.

```lua
os.locate("file_name1", ...)
```
sections.parameters: `file_name` is file name for which to search. It may contain some path information, e.g `xcode/xcode.lua`.
sections.returns: The full path to the first file found, or nil if the files could not be located.

sections.description:
Perform a wildcard match to locate one or more directories.

```lua
matches = os.matchdirs("pattern")
```
sections.parameters: `pattern` is the file system path to search. It may contain single (non-recursive) or double (recursive) asterisk wildcard patterns.
sections.returns: A list of directories which match the specified pattern. May be empty.
sections.examples:
```lua
matches = os.matchdirs("src/*")      -- non-recursive match
matches = os.matchdirs("src/**")     -- recursive match

matches = os.matchdirs("src/test*")  -- may also match partial names
```

sections.description:
Perform a wildcard match to locate one or more files.

```lua
matches = os.matchfiles("pattern")
```
sections.parameters: `pattern` is the file system path to search. It may contain single (non-recursive) or double (recursive) asterisk wildcard patterns.
sections.returns: A list of files which match the specified pattern. May be empty.
sections.examples:
```lua
matches = os.matchfiles("src/*.c")   -- non-recursive match
matches = os.matchfiles("src/**.c")  -- recursive match
```

sections.description:
Creates a new file system directory.

```lua
os.mkdir("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be created.
sections.returns: True if successful, otherwise nil and an error message.

sections.description:
Runs a shell command and return the output.

```lua
result, errorCode = os.outputof("command")
```
sections.parameters: `command` is a shell command to run.
sections.returns: The output and error code of the command.
sections.examples:
```lua
-- Get the ID for the host processor architecture
local proc = os.outputof("uname -p")
```

sections.description:
Searches a collection of paths for a particular file.

```lua
p = os.pathsearch("fname", "path1", ...)
```
sections.parameters:
`fname` is the name of the file being searched. This is followed by one or more path sets to be searched.

Path sets match the format of the PATH environment variable: a colon-delimited list of paths. On Windows, you may use a semicolon-delimited list if drive letters might be included.
sections.returns: The path to the directory which contains the file, if found. Otherwise, nil.

sections.description:
Returns the canonical absolute path of a filename.

```lua
ok, err = os.realpath(path)
```

This functions calls [realpath()](http://linux.die.net/man/3/realpath) on Posix systems and [_fullpath](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/506720ff.aspx) on Windows.
sections.parameters: `path` is the path to be converted.
sections.returns: If successful, returns the canonical absolute path. On error, returns nil and an error message.

sections.description:
Remove files from the file system.

```lua
os.remove("path", ...)
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be removed. Wildcard matches are supported, see [os.matchfiles](os.matchfiles.md) for examples.
sections.returns: True if successful, otherwise nil and an error message.
sections.examples:
```lua
local ok, err = os.remove{"**.bak", "**.log"}
if not ok then
	error(err)
end
```

sections.description:
Rename file system files or directories.

```lua
os.rename("path", "newpath")
```
sections.parameters:
`path` is the file system path to be renamed.
`newpath` is the renamed file system path.
sections.returns: True if successful, otherwise nil and an error message.
sections.examples:
```lua
local ok, err = os.rename{"file.bak", "file.log"}
if not ok then
	error(err)
end
```

sections.description:
Removes an existing directory as well as any files or subdirectories it contains.

```lua
os.rmdir("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be removed.
sections.returns: True if successful, otherwise nil and an error message.

sections.description:
Function retrieves information about a file.

```lua
info = os.stat("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to the file for which to retrieve information.
sections.returns:
If successful, a table of values:

| Field | Description                 |
|-------|-----------------------------|
| mtime | Last modified timestamp     |
| size  | The file size in bytes      |

sections.description:
Returns the name of the operating system currently being targeted.
See [system](system.md) for a complete list of OS identifiers.

The targeted OS may be overridden on the command line with the `--os` option.
```
$ premake5 --os=macosx xcode4
```
sections.examples:
```lua
print("Target os: " .. os.target())
```

sections.description:
Returns the id of the architecture currently being targeted.
See [architecture](architecture.md) for a complete list of architecture identifiers.

```lua
id = os.targetarch()
```

This will return `nil` by default instead of returning the architecture for the current running
system due to backwards compatibility.

A target architecture can be set either via setting [_TARGET_ARCH](globals/premake_TARGET_ARCH.md) or
by passing an architecture via the `--arch` command line option (which has the most priority).
sections.returns:
An architecture identifier; see [architecture()](architecture.md) for a complete list of identifiers.

Note that this function returns the architecture for the OS that Premake is generating files for, which is not necessarily the same as the architecture for the OS that Premake is currently running on.
sections.examples:
```lua
print(os.targetarch())
-- "x86_64"
end
```

sections.description:
Updates the last modified date of a file without changing its contents.

```lua
ok, err = os.touchfile("filename")
```
sections.parameters: `filename` is the file system path to the target file.
sections.returns: True if successful, otherwise nil and an error message.

sections.description:
Translate [command tokens](Tokens.md#command-tokens) into their OS or action specific equivalents.

```lua
cmd = os.translateCommands("cmd", map)
```
sections.parameters:
`cmd` is the command line to be translated. May be a single string or an array of strings.

`map` is either an [OS identifier](system.md) (e.g. "windows") to use one of Premake's built-in token mappings, or a table containing a custom mapping. If omitted, the currently targeted OS identifier will be used.
sections.returns: A new command line string with all command tokens replaced.
sections.examples:
```lua
-- translate for the currently targeted OS
cmd = os.translateCommands("{COPY} file1.txt file2.txt")

-- translate for a specific OS
cmd = os.translateCommands("{COPY} file1.txt file2.txt", "windows")

-- translate using a custom map
cmd = os.translateCommands("{COPY} file1.txt file2.txt", {
	copy = function(v)
		return "dup " .. v
	end
})
```

sections.description:
Returns a [Universally Unique Identifier](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UUID).

```lua
id = os.uuid(name)
```
sections.parameters: `name` is an optional string value. If provided, it will be used to create a deterministic, hash-based identifier.
sections.returns: A new UUID, a string value with the format 74CFC033-FA4D-4B1E-A871-7DC48FA36769.

sections.description:
Writes a string to a file, if the string differs from the current version of the file.

```lua
ok, err = os.writefile_ifnotequal("text", "filename")
```
sections.parameters:
`text` is the string to be written to the file.

`filename` is the file system path to the target file.
sections.returns: True if successful, otherwise nil and an error message.

sections.description:
Appends an extension to a file path if it is not already present.

```lua
p = path.appendExtension(p, ext)
```
sections.parameters:
`p` is a file system path.

`ext` is the extension to append to the path.
sections.returns: A new file system path with the extension appended, if it was not already part of the path.

sections.description:
Converts a relative path to an absolute path.

```lua
p = path.getabsolute("path", "relativeTo")
```
sections.parameters:
`path` is the relative path to be converted. It does not need to actually exist on the file system.

If provided, `relativeTo` specifies an absolute path from which `path` is considered relative. If not specified, the current working directory will be used.
sections.returns: A new absolute path, calculated from the current working directory, or the `relativeTo` parameter if provided.
sections.availability: Premake 4.0 or later. The `relativeTo` parameter is available in Premake 5.0 or later.

sections.description:
Returns the base file portion of a path, with the directory and file extension removed.

```lua
p = path.getbasename("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be split.
sections.returns: The base name portion of the supplied path, with any directory and file extension removed.

sections.description:
Returns the directory portion of a path, with any file name removed.

```lua
p = path.getdirectory("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be split.
sections.returns: The directory portion of the path, with any file name removed. If the path does not include any directory information, the "." (single dot) current directory is returned.

sections.description:
Returns the drive letter portion of a path, if present.

```lua
p = path.getdrive("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be split.
sections.returns: The drive letter portion of the path, if one is specified. Otherwise, nil.

sections.description:
Returns the file extension portion of a path.

```lua
p = path.getextension("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be split.
sections.returns: The file extension portion of the path, or an empty string if no extension is present.

sections.description:
Returns the file name and extension, with any directory information removed.

```lua
p = path.getname("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be split.
sections.returns: The file name and extension, with no directory information.

sections.description:
The **path.getrelative** function computes a relative path from one directory to another.

```lua
p = path.getrelative("src", "dest")
```
sections.parameters: `src` is the originating directory, `dest` is the target directory. Both may be specified as absolute or relative to the current working directory. The paths do not need to exist on the file system.
sections.returns: A relative path from `src` to `dest`.

sections.description:
Returns true if a file system path has the given file extension.

```lua
path.hasextension("path", "ext")
```
sections.parameters:
`path` is the file system path to be tested.

`ext` is the file extension to check. May be a single string or an array of strings.
sections.returns: True if `path` matches any of the provided file extensions.

sections.description:
Determines if a given file system path is absolute.

```lua
path.isabsolute("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to check.
sections.returns: True if the file system path is absolute, false otherwise. The tests include checking for a leading forward or backward slash, a dollar sign (indicating a environment variable), or a DOS drive letter.

sections.description:
Returns true if the specified path represents a C source code file, based on its file extension.

```lua
path.iscfile("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be tested.
sections.returns: True if the path matches a well-known C file extension, which currently includes `.c`, `.s`, and `.m`.

sections.description:
Returns true if the specified path represents a C++ source code file, based on its file extension.

```lua
path.iscppfile("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be tested.
sections.returns: True if the path matches a well-known C file extension, which currently includes `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`, `.c`, `.s`, `.m`, and `.mm`.

sections.description:
Returns true if the specified path represents a C++ header file, based on its file extension.

```lua
path.iscppheader("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be tested.
sections.returns: True if the path matches a well-known C file extension, which currently includes `.h`, `.hh`, `.hpp`, and `.hxx`.

sections.description:
Returns true if the specified path represents a Cocoa framework bundle, based on its file extension.

```lua
path.isframework("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be tested.
sections.returns: True if the path matches has a **.framework** extension.

sections.description:
Returns true if the specified path represents a file that can be linked against, based on its file extension.

```lua
path.islinkable("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be tested.
sections.returns: True if the path matches a well-known linkable file extension, which currently includes `.o`, `.obj`, `.a`, `.lib`, and `.so`.

sections.description:
Returns true if the specified path represents an object file, based on its file extension.

```lua
path.isobjectfile("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be tested.
sections.returns: True if the path matches a well-known object file extension, which currently includes `.o` and `.obj`.

sections.description:
Returns true if the specified path represents a Windows resource file, based on its file extension.

```lua
path.isresourcefile("path")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to be tested.
sections.returns: True if the path matches has an **.rc** extension.

sections.description:
Joins two path portions together into a single path.

```lua
path.join("leading", "trailing", ...)
```

If trailing is an absolute path, then the leading portion is ignored, and the absolute path is returned instead (see below for examples).
sections.parameters: `leading` is the beginning portion of the path; `trailing` is a portion to be merged. Multiple arguments may be specified, which will be joined in the order provided.
sections.returns: A merged path.
sections.examples:
```lua
-- returns "MyWorkspace/MyProject"
p = path.join("MyWorkspace", "MyProject")

-- returns "/usr/bin", because the trailing path is absolute
p = path.join("MyWorkspace", "/usr/bin")

-- tokens are assumed to be absolute; this returns "$(ProjectDir)"
p = path.join("MyWorkspace", "$(ProjectDir)")
```

sections.description:
Tries to create a clean file system representation of a path.

```lua
path.normalize("path")
```

Normalization includes removing duplicate and trailing slashes, leading "./" sequences, and filtering out "../" sequences where possible.
sections.parameters: `path` is the path to be normalized.
sections.returns: The normalized path.

sections.description:
Takes a path which is relative to one location and makes it relative to another location instead.

```lua
path.rebase("relative_path", "old_base", "new_base")
```
sections.parameters:
`relative_path` is a file system path, specified relative to `old_base`, which is to be rebased.

`new_base` is the location from which it should be made relative.
sections.returns: A relative path from *new_base*.

sections.description:
Replace the file extension.

```lua
path.replaceextension("path", "new_extension")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path on which the extension should be replaced. `new_extension` is the replacement file extension.
sections.returns: A new file system path with the replaced extension.

sections.description:
Converts the file separators in a path.

```lua
path.translate("path", "newsep")
```
sections.parameters: `path` is the file system path to translate; `newsep` is the new path separator. If `newsep` is not specified a Windows-style backslash is assumed.
sections.returns: The translated path.

sections.description:
Converts from Premake's simple wildcard syntax to a corresponding Lua pattern.

```lua
p = path.wildcards("pattern")
```
sections.parameters: `pattern` is a file system path which may contain one more `\*` (shallow match) or `\*\*` (recursive match) sequences.
sections.returns: A Lua pattern string which is equivalent to the input pattern.

sections.description:
Capitalizes the first letter of a string.

```lua
s = string.capitalized("s")
```
sections.parameters: `s` is the string value to be capitalized.
sections.returns: The input string with the first letter capitalized.

sections.description:
Returns true if the string contains the specified substring.

```lua
string.contains("haystack", "needle")
```
sections.parameters:
`haystack` is the string to be tested.

`needle` is the substring for which to search. Lua patterns are not supported.
sections.returns: True if `haystack` contains `needle`.

sections.description:
Returns true if the given string ends with the provided sequence.

```lua
string.endswith("haystack", "needle")
```
sections.parameters: `haystack` is the string to check. `needle` is the ending sequence to check against.
sections.returns: True if haystack ends with needle.

sections.description:
Escapes the string for use in Lua patterns. Escapes the following characters `( ) . % + - * ? [ ] ^ $` with `%`.

```lua
escaped = string.escapepattern("s")
```
sections.parameters: `s` is the string to escape.
sections.returns: Returns the input string escaped for use in Lua patterns.
sections.examples:
```lua
local match = filename:match(string.escapepattern("boost_filesystem-vc140.1.61.0.0"))
```

sections.description:
Returns an array of strings, each of which is a substring formed by splitting on the provided pattern.

```lua
parts = string.explode("str", "pattern")
```
sections.parameters: `str` is the string to be split. *pattern* is the separator pattern at which to split; it may use Lua's pattern matching syntax.
sections.returns: A list of substrings.
sections.examples:
```lua
e = "a\nmulti\nline\nstring\n"
> for k,v in next, string.explode(e, "\n") do print(k, v) end
1	a
2	multi
3	line
4	string
5
```

sections.description:
Finds the last instance of a pattern within a string.

```lua
string.findlast("str", "pattern", plain)
```
sections.parameters: `str` is the string to be searched. `pattern` is the pattern to search for; it may use Lua's pattern matching syntax. If `plain` is true, no pattern matching will be performed (faster).
sections.returns: The matching pattern, if found, or nil if there were no matches.

sections.description:
Returns a [DBJ2 hash](http://www.cse.yorku.ca/~oz/hash.html) of a string value.

```lua
string.hash("value")
```
sections.parameters: `value` is the string value to be hashed.
sections.returns: The DBJ2 hash value of the provided string.

sections.description:
Returns the number of lines of text contained by the string.

```lua
string.lines("str")
```
sections.parameters: `str` is the string to be tested.
sections.returns: The number of lines of text contained by the string.

sections.description:
Returns a plural version of the provided string.

```lua
pl = string.plural("str")
```
sections.parameters: `str` is the string to be made plural.
sections.returns: A plural version of the provided string.
sections.examples:
```lua
-- returns "projects"
pl = string.plural("project")

-- returns "stories"
pl = string.plural("story")
```

sections.description:
Returns a [SHA-1 hash](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-1) of a string value.

```lua
string.sha1("value")
```
sections.parameters: `value` is the string value to be hashed.
sections.returns: The SHA-1 hash value of the provided string.

sections.description:
Returns true if the given string starts with the provided sequence.

```lua
string.startswith("haystack", "needle")
```
sections.parameters: `haystack` is the string to check. `needle` is the starting sequence to check against.
sections.returns: True if haystack starts with needle.

sections.description:
Make a copy of the indexed elements of the table.

```lua
copy = table.arraycopy(tbl)
```
sections.parameters: `tbl` is the table to be copied.
sections.returns: A new table containing the indexed elements of the provided table.

sections.description:
Determines if an array contains a particular value.

```lua
table.contains(arr, value)
```
sections.parameters: `arr` is a table containing indexed elements. *value* is the value for which to search.
sections.returns: True if the array contains the value, false otherwise.

sections.description:
Make a complete copy of a table, including any child tables it contains.

```lua
copy = table.deepcopy(tbl)
```
sections.parameters: `tbl` is the table to be copied.
sections.returns: A copy of the provided table.

sections.description:
Enumerates an array of objects and returns a new table containing only the value of one particular field.


```lua
table.extract(arr, "key")
```
sections.parameters: `arr` is an array of tables. `key` is the name of the field to be extracted.
sections.returns: A new array containing only the values of the provided field key.

sections.description:
Removes empty strings or nil values from an array, in place.

```lua
table.filterempty(arr)
```
sections.parameters: `arr` is the array of values to be filtered.
sections.returns: Returns `arr` with any empty strings or nil values removed.

sections.description:
Flattens a hierarchy of arrays into a single array containing all of the values.

```lua
table.flatten(arr)
```
sections.parameters: `arr` is an table containing indexed values, which may themselves also contain indexed values.
sections.returns: A new array containing all of the elements, nested or otherwise.

sections.description:
Merge two lists into an array of objects containing pairs of values, one from each list.


```lua
table.fold(arr1, arr2)
```
sections.parameters: `arr1` and `arr2` are tables containing indexed values.
sections.returns: A new array of objects containing the corresponding elements from each list.

sections.description:
Walk the elements of an array and call the specified function for each non-nil element.

```lua
table.foreachi(arr, fn)
```
sections.parameters: `arr` is an table containing indexed values. `fn` is the function to call for each non-nil element. The value (not the index) will be passed as the only argument.

sections.description:
Merges an array of items into a single, formatted string.

```lua
table.implode(arr, "before", "after", "between")
```
sections.parameters: `arr` is the array to be converted into a string. `before` is a string to be inserted before each item. `after` is a string to be inserted after each item. `between` is a string to be inserted between items.
sections.returns: The formatted string.

sections.description:
Returns the key or index of a value within a table.

```lua
table.indexof(arr, value)
```
sections.parameters: `arr` is a table containing indexed elements. `value` is the value for which to search.
sections.returns: The key or index of the value if it is present in the table; nil otherwise.

sections.description:
Insert a new value into a table at the index after the specified existing value. If the specified value does not exist in the table, the new value is appended to the end of the table.


```lua
table.insertafter(arr, after, value)
```
sections.parameters: `arr` is a table containing indexed elements. `after` is the value to insert after. `value` is the value to insert.

sections.description:
Inserts a value of array of values into a table. If the value is itself a table, its contents are enumerated and added instead.

```lua
table.insertflat(arr, values)
```
sections.parameters: `arr` is a table containing indexed elements. `values` is a value or array of values to insert.
sections.returns: Returns `arr` with the new values added in place.

sections.description:
Returns true if the table is empty, and contains no indexed or keyed values.


```lua
table.isempty(tbl)
```
sections.parameters: `tbl` is the table to be tested.
sections.returns: True if the table is empty.

sections.description:
Adds the values from one array to the end of another and returns the result.


```lua
table.join(arr1, arr2, ...)
```
sections.parameters: `arr1` contains the elements to be placed at the front of the result, followed by the elements of `arr2` and so on.
sections.returns: A new array containing all of the values in order.

sections.description:
Return an array of all keys used in a table.

```lua
table.keys(tbl)
```
sections.parameters: `tbl` is the table to be enumerated.
sections.returns: A new array containing all of the keys encountered in the table.

sections.description:
Adds the key-value associations from one table into another and returns the resulting merged table.

```lua
table.merge(tbl1, tbl2, ...)
```
sections.parameters: One or more tables to be merged.
sections.returns: A new table containing the key-value pairs from each input table, from first to last.

sections.description:
Replace all instances of `value` with `replacement` in an array. Array elements are modified in place.

```lua
table.replace(tbl, value, replacement)
```
sections.parameters: `tbl` is the table to be modified. `value` is the value to be replaced, and `replacement` is the new value to use.
sections.returns: Returns `tbl`, modified in place with the replacement values.

sections.description:
Converts the contents of a table to a formatted string.

```lua
table.tostring(tbl, recurse)
```
sections.parameters:
- `tbl` is the table to be formatted.
- *recurse* is an optional integer indicating the depth of recursion
sections.returns: A string representing the formatted contents of the table.

sections.description:
Translates the values contained in array, using the specified translation table, and returns the results in a new array.

```lua
table.translate(arr, translation)
```
sections.parameters: `arr` is the array of values to be translated. *translation* is a key-value table containing the replacement values, or a function taking a single value and returning the translation.
sections.returns: Returns a new array containing the translated values.

sections.description:
Clears the console from the cursor location to the end of the line.

```lua
term.clearToEndOfLine()
```
sections.examples:
``` lua
term.clearToEndOfLine()
```

sections.description:
Retrieves the current color setting of text printed to the console

```lua
term.getTextColor()
```
sections.returns: The current color setting. One of the color values listed in [term.setTextColor](term.setTextColor.md)
sections.examples:
``` lua
local currentColor = term.getTextColor()
print("Current color setting is: " .. currentColor)
```

sections.description:
Moves the console cursor left by a number of columns.

```lua
term.moveLeft(columns)
```
sections.parameters: `columns` is the number of columns to move left.
sections.examples:
``` lua
term.moveLeft(2)
```

sections.description:
Returns the current console color setting and restores the previously saved color setting saved by the last call of [term.pushColor](term.pushColor.md)

``` lua
term.popColor()
```
sections.returns:
* `nil` if the color stack is empty.
* The current color setting. One of the color values listed in [term.setTextColor](term.setTextColor.md)
sections.examples:
``` lua
local currentColor = term.popColor()
print("Last color setting was: " .. currentColor)
```

sections.description:
Saves the current text color state and changes the color of future text printed to the console.
Use [term.popColor](term.popColor.md) to restore the previous color setting.

``` lua
term.pushColor(color)
```
sections.parameters: * `color` - See the listing in [term.setTextColor](term.setTextColor.md)
sections.examples:
``` lua
-- set text to green
term.pushColor(term.green)
print("Hello World")
```

sections.description:
Changes the color of future text printed to the console

```lua
term.setTextColor(color)
```
sections.parameters:
`color` - One of:
  * `nil` (default color)
  * term.black
  * term.blue
  * term.green
  * term.cyan
  * term.red
  * term.purple
  * term.brown
  * term.lightGray
  * term.gray
  * term.lightBlue
  * term.lightGreen
  * term.lightCyan
  * term.lightRed
  * term.magenta
  * term.yellow
  * term.white

For specific purposes the following can be used/overridden:
  * term.warningColor
  * term.errorColor
  * term.infoColor
sections.examples:
Print text in green

```lua
term.setTextColor(term.green)
print("Hello World")
```

sections.description:
```lua
zip.extract(sourceZip, destinationDir)
```
sections.parameters:
- `sourceZip` is the zip file which has to be extracted
- `destinationDir` is the destination directory for the extracted files
